subject: Proposal: capacity-reserve + rate-cap option for renewal
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@atlashealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — interest in multi-year advance credit / rate protection

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well. We’re starting renewal planning for our LLM footprint at Atlas and want to explore options to avoid the mid-year price increases we saw last cycle. Specifically, two asks:

- A multi-year (2–3 year) advance-credit or prepay structure that gives us predictable unit pricing.
- A rate-protection mechanism (rate cap or guarantee) so we don’t see upward movement during the term.

Our target is to keep net per-token spend flat and preferably reduce ~10–20% vs current list. We have predictable but growth-heavy usage — estimated 1.2x YOY. Billing preference: annual upfront if we can secure a price cap.

Can you share what Redwood can offer and any draft terms/agreement language we should expect? Also looping Marco (finance) and procurement.

Thanks,
Ellen
Procurement Lead, Atlas Health
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@atlashealth.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — interest in multi-year advance credit / rate protection

Ellen —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a starting term sheet that walks through a capacity-reserve (advance-credit pool) + rate-protection addendum. High level options we can do today:

1) Annual prepay (1 year) — up to 12% off list for 100% upfront annual commitment, with a 6-month credit buffer for unexpected spikes.
2) Layered multi-year reserve (3-year example) — Year1: 60% prepay, Year2: 25% prepay, Year3: 15% prepay. In exchange for the 3-year commit we can offer an 18% blended discount off list plus a formal Rate Protection Addendum that caps per-token list increases at +3%/yr.
3) Full 3-year upfront — 22% off list if Atlas pays 100% at signature (rare but available for very large, committed TCV).

We designed the layered reserve to align with growth (less upfront in later years) while still delivering predictable economics. Billing can be annual upfront invoices tied to the prepay amounts you choose. We can also structure a PO+annual invoice workflow if procurement prefers.

I’ve attached: Redwood_CapacityReserve_TermSheet_v1.pdf and RateProtection_Addendum.docx and a short Usage_Playbook template. I’ll loop Finance and Legal for contract language tweaks.

Next steps: If any of the above looks promising, tell me which option (1/2/3) you prefer and your preferred prepay % by year and I’ll produce a signature-ready term sheet/DocuSign.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@atlashealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@atlashealth.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 10:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — interest in multi-year advance credit / rate protection

Marissa —

Thanks — this is helpful. Quick clarifying questions from finance:

- For the layered multi-year reserve (option 2), can you confirm the invoicing cadence? We want annual invoices, not a single 3-year invoice.
- If we commit to the Year1 60% prepay but growth exceeds forecasts and we consume more, do you offer any carry-forward credit or flexible top-ups mid-year?
- Legal will want the Rate Protection Addendum to include an explicit exclusion for changes in law (e.g., tariffs or regulatory fees) — is that standard?

We also would like to see a sample invoice and a draft PO workflow so our AP team can sign off.

Marco
VP Finance, Atlas Health
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@atlashealth.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@atlashealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 08:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — interest in multi-year advance credit / rate protection

Marco — thanks, good questions. Quick responses and proposed modifications:

- Invoicing: We will split the multi-year reserve into annual invoices (Year1 invoice at signature for the 60% Year1 prepay; Year2 and Year3 invoices can be issued on each anniversary). We’ll put the payment schedule in the term sheet.

- Consumption overages / top-ups: Yes — we support mid-term top-ups. Any usage beyond the prepay pool will be billed at the agreed blended unit price for the term, or you can purchase an incremental top-up at list price and we’ll credit it back against future invoices under the same blended discount schedule. We’ll document the carry-forward and top-up rules in Section 4 of the term sheet.

- Exclusions in Rate Protection: Standard practice is to exclude changes required by law or third-party pass-throughs (cloud provider surcharges, newly imposed taxes). We can add explicit language to the addendum to protect both parties.

Internal ask for Vivek/Ben/Evelyn: can we approve the proposed 18% blended discount for the 3-year layered option and the +3%/yr cap? Also confirm we’re comfortable allowing annual invoicing for the layered option and providing the top-up/carry-forward language as described. I’ve attached the sample invoice mockup and a PO workflow example to the Drive link.

Thanks — Marissa

-- Forwarded attachment: Redwood_CapacityReserve_TermSheet_v1.pdf (pdf)
-- Forwarded attachment: RateProtection_Addendum.docx (docx)
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — interest in multi-year advance credit / rate protection

Marissa / team —

18% blended discount for the proposed 3-year layered reserve looks reasonable given Atlas’s size and growth profile. Approve with the following guardrails:

- Add a usage review cadence (quarterly) tied to a mutual action plan; if YOY usage diverges >25%, allow a re-rate discussion or structured top-up that preserves the rate-protection for already-prepaid units.
- Keep the +3%/yr cap but add a carve-out for pass-through costs (cloud provider pricing changes).
- Approve annual invoicing for Year2/Year3 (no single up-front for full 3-year unless customer requests it).

Ben/Evelyn, once we have the final terms, send to Legal for a quick redline and prepare a DocuSign package. Marissa, please confirm and I’ll greenlight the term sheet to go to Atlas.

— Vivek
CTO (covering commercial approvals)
